newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl says 2.5 pct 1997 German growth possible.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says 2.5 pct 1997 German growth possible.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl said the German economy showed a pleasant level of economic growth in the first quarter, and that the government's target of 2.5 percent growth for the full year was attainable.
Kohl added however, that the government's goal of halving unemployment by the year 2000 may not be possible.
On European monetary union (EMU), Kohl said critics who say the single currency should be delayed should consider the effects this would have on the mark and on German exports.
Kohl says 2.5 pct 1997 German growth possible
"Growth in the first quarter was pleasing. For 1997 as a whole, 2.5 percent is attainable," Kohl said at the Dresdner Bank's 125th anniversary.
But the labour market situation was improving only slowly, Kohl said.
"The goal of halving unemployment by the year 2000 may not be achievable. But to give up the goal now would mean not to achieve anything on the labour market," he said.
Kohl said the government's proposal to revalue the Bundesbank's gold reserves did not represent an attack on the central bank's independence.

Earlier, Kohl's office denied a newspaper report that he had threatened to resign several times last week during budget negotiations between his Christian Democrats and their coalition partners the Free Democrats.
